title: VPC security synthesis module: consolidated SG/NACL/PrivateDNS + egress guardrail
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: provide a single, opinionated Terraform module that stitches security groups, network ACLs, private Route53 zones/resolvers, and egress guardrails into a reusable, upgrade-safe building block for Private (VPC) deployments. Scope: - Security groups with least-privilege templates (control plane, inference nodes, metrics/telemetry). - NACLs for subnet-level hardening with sane default deny/allow windows for burst traffic. - Private Hosted Zones + Route53 Resolver endpoints + conditional forwarding for customer privatelink/topology. - Policy-driven egress allowing whitelists, enforced proxy endpoints, and fallback behavior (deny/alert). - Built-in health checks and a lightweight diagnostics plan (terraform plan output annotations + post-apply smoke tests). Non-goals: - Replacing customer-specific custom firewall appliances. - Full service-mesh integration (we will provide hooks).

acceptance_criteria: Module is published to internal Terraform registry with semver tags and upgrade notes
Default configuration enforces deny-by-default egress and documents explicit allowlist procedure
Private Hosted Zone creation + Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints are optional and can be toggled at deploy time
Automated post-apply checks confirm: resolution of private zone records, resolver endpoints reachable from designated subnets, and egress proxy reachable
Module has automation for safe stateful NACL changes (small roll step guidance) and docs for in-place upgrades
Integration tests pass in CI: plan/apply/destroy in sandbox job; terraform drift test passes for 3 sample VPC topologies
testing_and_rollout: Unit tests: terraform validate + terratest harness for SG/NACL permutations (run in CI)
Stage rollout: apply to privnet-qa (canary) with monitor window 48h; observe metrics and alerts
Gradual expansion: apply to 3 non-critical customer-like VPCs, then to Dedicated infra pool during low-traffic window
Rollback plan: terraform apply using previous module version + restore known-good security group IDs; Ops runbook located: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Privnet+Security+Rollback
Post-apply verification: run smoke.sh in repo which returns JSON checklist and posts to #infra-deployments Slack channel
implementation_notes: Design choices: use security group templates (control plane, worker, metrics) instead of per-service SG proliferation to simplify rule audits
NACLs will be applied per-subnet with a generated rule priority strategy to avoid rule overlap; document trade-offs vs stateful SGs
Private DNS: support both hosted-zone-plus-peering and resolver-endpoint patterns; provide variables to opt between them
Egress policy: two-layer approach — Route level (NACL + SG) for hard deny and a policy table for allowlist + optional proxy endpoint enforced via outbound rule
Upgrade strategy: publish migration guide and automated 'upgrade-plan' script that does dry-run checks and flags destructive NACL/SG operations
Telemetry: emit terraform plan annotations to a small Lambda that parses for 'destructive' changes and creates a GitHub issue if risky
Secrets: require customer to provide KMS key ARN for any private-zone record updates; module will not store plaintext credentials
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: NACL changes can cause intermittent connectivity loss during reorder. Mitigation: automated plan shows exact numeric rule changes and apply guidance; schedule maintenance window for high-risk customers
Risk: Misconfigured private DNS could break internal service discovery. Mitigation: include a built-in resolver test and an option to run DNS verification before route propagation
Risk: Egress allowlist too permissive by default. Mitigation: default is deny-all with a small pre-populated operational allowlist (monitor-only) until customer explicitly approves additions
Risk: Terraform state drift between module versions. Mitigation: add clear state migration docs and CI job that simulates upgrade against snapshot states
